# What Stan cost us

## The integral solver would not hold

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```
Chain 252 Exception: Error in function
tanh_sinh<double>::integrate: The tanh_sinh
quadrature evaluated your function at a singular
point and got -0.038716888888388652. Integration
bounds were automatically narrowed, but the
integral was found to be increasing at the new
endpoint. ...

Warning: 243 chain(s) finished unexpectedly!
```

- **243 of 256** chains, dying after warmup, in the middle of sampling
- A day of tolerances, boundary fractions and midpoint approximations
  got that to **70 of 600**
- `integrate_1d` errors rather than rejecting, and there is no
  `try`/`catch` to wrap it in
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```stan
// before
result = integrate_1d(
  primary_censored_integrand, lower_bound, d,
  theta, {d, pwindow}, ids, 1e-2
);

// after
result = ode_rk45(
  primary_censored_ode, y0, lower_bound, {d},
  theta, {d, pwindow}, ids
)[1, 1];
```

- Recast as an ODE, **0 of 600**
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
epinowcast/primarycensored#34 and PR #64, commit `1c4e6f1`, September
2024. Nine days from opening the issue to merging the ODE recast. Also
reported four to five times faster, from one run rather than a
benchmark.
:::

## No user types, so distributions became integers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```r
dist_id <- pcd_stan_dist_id(family_name)

stanvars_functions[[1]]$scode <- gsub(
  "dist_id", dist_id,
  stanvars_functions[[1]]$scode,
  fixed = TRUE
)
```

::: {.attribution}
`epidist/R/marginal_model.R:339-347`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- The type parameter is an integer, pushed into Stan source as text,
  from another language
- **`dist_id = 3` meant Normal in Stan and Weibull in R.** On the
  numerical path, which is anything outside gamma, lognormal and
  Weibull with a uniform primary, asking for a Weibull fitted a normal
  and returned numbers
- The two integer tables agreed on lognormal, gamma and exponential,
  and on nothing else
- The fix came with a **228 line test** whose only job is checking that
  two integer tables agree
:::
::::

::: {.callout-important}
`primary_censored(Weibull(2, 1), Uniform(0, 1))` carries the type. There
is no second table for it to disagree with.
:::
